newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela inflation to blip-up on min wage-Petkoff.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela inflation to blip-up on min wage-Petkoff.

text.p: Venezuelan Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff acknowledged Wednesday that an impending minimum wage hike will drive up inflation over the short term, but he stuck to the government's official 35 percent inflation target for calendar year 1997.
The new minimum wage of 75,000 bolivars ($155) per month, compared to current minimum take home pay of 52,000 bolivars, is due to be signed into law by President Rafael Caldera Thursday.

"When the private sector raises salaries -- as it should once the (new) minimum salary is made law ... then there clearly should be another hop in the inflation rate," Petkoff said in a radio interview.

Petkoff did not forecast how much impact the new wage would exercise on June inflation. But he said the rise in May inflation to 3.1 percent from 2.4 percent in April was largely due to a 75 percent public sector pay rise granted in February.
